eligibility.quote: Reporter: "Only encountered this once, so it is difficult to say how to reproduce it. Possibly just repeated runs of CI will do it."; maintainer mikeferguson: "I notice in the logs \"terminate called without an active exception\" - which usually means that a std::thread went out of scope while not joined/stopped - I notice we have a std::thread in this test - but I don't actually see how it could go out of scope..."; maintainer henningkayser: "Maybe it really was an unrelated threading issue somewhere..." ... "closing for now"

loudness.quote: Actual behaviour: Test appears to fail inconsistently

resolution.quote: henningkayser: "I haven't seen this one lately. Are we still running into this? Maybe it really was an unrelated threading issue somewhere..." ... "closing for now" — closed without a fix; the packet's PR #1458 is a Mergify backport of #1266, not a fix of this test.

notes: Independently verified: issue #1334 body (title "CI: RDF loader test is flaky"; the quoted non-reproducibility line and "Test appears to fail inconsistently"); the four maintainer comments quoted in the spec (mikeferguson's std::thread diagnosis verbatim, including his link to PR #1384 as a similar instance he fixed elsewhere; henningkayser's doubt and "closing for now"); the test file at 58f3828224f051b40ce0b66d217ae4335703a5d2 (L79 "std::thread spinning_thread([&executor] { executor.spin(); });", L85-88 ASSERT_NE on loader.getURDF()/getSRDF(), L90 "spinning_thread.join();") matching the spec's notes about the ASSERT-before-join structure; the CI run link now returns Not Found with HTTP status 404 via the GitHub API for both ros-planning/moveit2 and moveit/moveit2 paths, matching the spec's claim; PR #1458's body shows it is an automatic Mergify backport of #1266 — consistent with the spec's characterization that the fix_refs are unrelated PRs whose CI hit the flaky test. My independent reading: no two interacting units are named by any source; the only diagnosis points inside the test process's own std::thread lifecycle, and no root cause or fix was ever identified — E1's requirement of one concrete defect is not met and no boundary-crossing element is documented, so ineligible is correct. Minor nuance, not a disagreement: with a single unit the strict tree walk stops at step 1; the spec records step 2 'internal' and documents the reasoning, which reaches the same ineligible outcome.
